wu: Article Race: Write 'a/an/the' on the board. Students stand in teams. You say a school phrase like 'I like ___ science class.' Teams race to grab the correct article card and place it in the blank. First correct team gets a point.
wuAlt: Subject Charades: Students mime a school subject (e.g., 'math' by writing numbers, 'art' by painting). Others guess, 'Is it ___ art?'
Quick Quiz: Flashcards of school subjects. Students say 'I like ___ geography' or 'I don't like ___ history' with correct articles.
pres: Use a spooky school poster. Point to subjects: 'Look, ___ science lab has a ghost! I like ___ science because it's interesting.' Drill 'I like/don't like + [article] + subject + because + [article] + reason.' Check with thumbs up/down: 'Do you like ___ math?'
presAlt: Mystery Box: Put school object props (book, ruler) in a box. Students pull one out and say, 'I like ___ ruler because it's useful.'
Video Clip: Show 1-min clip of a funny school scene. Pause and ask, 'What does he like? Does she like ___ PE?'
prac: Halloween Taboo: In pairs, students get cards with a school subject and taboo words. They describe it for their partner to guess, e.g., 'It's ___ subject. You need a pen. I like it because it's creative.' Partner must say, 'Is it ___ art?'
pracAlt: Article Dice Game: Roll a die. 1=a, 2=an, 3=the, 4=like, 5=don't like, 6=because. Students make a sentence with the words rolled, e.g., 'I like ___ history because ___ teacher is nice.'
Find Someone Who...: Students walk around asking, 'Do you like ___ science? Why?' and write names.
ls: Listen to a spooky school dialogue. Students fill in blanks with 'a/an/the': 'My friend hates ___ art class because ___ teacher is ___ ghost.' Check answers in pairs before class review.
re: Zombie Tag: One student is 'Zombie Teacher'. They chase others. If tagged, the student must say, 'I don't like ___ P.E. because it's hard!' before unfreezing. Game continues for 2 mins.
prod: Roleplay: 'The Haunted School'. In pairs, one student is a new kid, the other is a ghost guide. Guide says, 'Welcome to ___ school! I like ___ library because ___ books are magic.' New kid responds, 'Do you like ___ science? I don't like it because ___ lab is scary.'
rw: Read a short article about a spooky school event. Circle all 'a/an/the'. Then write 3 sentences about your own school using the same structure: 'I like ___ subject because ___ teacher is ___ kind person.'
st: Turn off lights. Read the spooky story chain paragraph by paragraph. End with, 'The ghost said, "I like ___ history because ___ past is full of secrets."' Close with: 'Today we talked about school subjects with articles. Thanks for your great ideas, goodbye!'
g: Teams grab 'a/an/the' cards for phrases like 'I like ___ math'
Describe school subjects without taboo words
Tagged students say 'I don't like ___ P.E.'
Ask 'Do you like ___ science?' and write names
Pull school objects and make sentences
diff: Fast finishers: Write a 4-line poem about a spooky school subject using articles
Support: Use a word bank with 'a/an/the' and subjects to build sentences
hw: Find a real article/video about school life and summarise it in 3 sentences
Write the ending of the class spooky story (6-8 lines)
Interview a family member about their school days and report back using 'I like/don't like... because...'
tip: Use the Halloween theme to make article practice memorable—ghosts love grammar! For Moroccan teens, connect to local school traditions like the baccalaureate to increase engagement.
